review_candidates.title: Operations Manager – Hospitals, Secondary and Specialist Care – East of England or London
review_candidates.description: Grade A - £55,172 (National) or £61,028 (London – for London office based or homebased workers within the boundary of the M25) – There is also an additional homeworking allowance of £600 per annum for those working from home. For part time roles – please note this will be pro rata. Contracted Hours: Full time 37 hours per week Contract Type: 1 x Permanent vacancy in East of England. 1 x Secondment opportunity until March 2028 in London Closing date: Sunday 22nd November 2026 at 11.59pm Interview dates: Monday 14th & Tuesday 15th December 2026 - Stratford Office This role requires regular travel across East of England or London areas as needed for meetings and engagement activities. Applicants must be willing and able to travel within this area. For this reason, we are seeking candidates who live within the specified regions. Location will be carefully considered to ensure the role and responsibilities remain manageable. Make a difference Every role at CQC contributes to our mission, if you’re looking for a new role in Operations – Hospitals, Secondary and Specialist Care that gives a true sense of meaning and purpose then you’ve found it! As an Operations Manager, you’ll lead a team of specialists to deliver high-quality assessments that help ensure people receive safe, effective, and compassionate care. Picture this Imagine leading a team that helps identify and address risks in health and care services – making a real difference to people’s lives every day. You’ll be part of a supportive, values-driven team that works together to improve care across the country. At CQC As An Operations Manager – Hospitals, Secondary And Specialist Care In The Operations Directorate, You Will Get The Chance To Lead a specialist HSSC team to deliver a complex system-based assessment that uncovers risks and drives improvements in care. Work collaboratively with other HSSC operational managers to identify and respond to risk and to schedule inspections across the network. Develop network wide ways of working in respect of HSSC services, developing consistency through procedures and processes Collaborate with data and insight teams to apply intelligence that shapes regulatory decisions and protects people using services. The role You’ll be key in helping us deliver our work. In this role, you’ll: Lead and support teams: Manage a team of inspectors, ensuring they have the tools, support, and development they need to succeed. Manage operational delivery: Oversee end-to-end assessment activity of HSSC services within the area and the wider network, ensuring it meets performance targets and regulatory standards. Collaborate and problem-solve: Work with colleagues across CQC including colleagues in mental health act operations and external partners to manage risk, respond to concerns, and drive improvements in care. Show Us We’ll be looking for the following skills, knowledge and experience in your application form: Significant experience and expertise in HSSC services. Experience leading operational delivery: You’ve successfully managed teams and delivered complex programmes or services, ideally in a HSSC setting. Ability to use insight to drive decisions: You’ve used data or evidence to inform actions, solve problems, or improve quality. Strong collaboration and communication skills: You’ve worked with a range of stakeholders – internally and externally including with NHS trusts – to influence outcomes and build effective partnerships. Compliance Note For Internal Candidates This is a secondment/fixed term opportunity. Please read the recruitment and selection policy section on secondments. You must discuss your application with your line manager before applying. Next steps If you apply, you’ll need to create a profile and complete an online application form. Your application will be completely anonymous. Please see our information for applicants for more details on the process. We contact every applicant to let them know the outcome of their application, so you will hear from us whether or not you are shortlisted. You can read the full details of the role in the Job Description If you’d like an informal chat about the role contact : East of England: Sarah Ivory-Donnelly, Deputy Director of Hospitals, Secondary and Specialist Healthcare Central Region - Sarah.Ivory-Donnelly@cqc.org.uk London: Antoinette Smith, Deputy Director of Hospitals, Secondary and Specialist Healthcare South Region - Antoinette.Smith@cqc.org.uk For general enquiries, please email recruitment@cqc.org.uk. The Benefits We offer a wide range of benefits, including: Annual leave starting at 27 days per year, rising to 32.5 days with service, plus bank holidays (usually 8 days per year). Training and development opportunities. Wellbeing initiatives, such as gym discounts and meditation. NHS pension scheme, with around 23.7% employer contribution. Discount schemes (including eligibility for a Blue Light card, at a cost of £4.99 and valid for 2 years), reward vouchers, car leasing and more! Please see our benefits page for the full list. Equity for all We know job descriptions can feel intimidating. Research shows they can cause some people to doubt whether they’re a good fit. This happens more often to people from underrepresented groups (e.g. ethnic minority backgrounds). If this role interests you, we encourage you to apply. Your unique perspective, skills, and experience could be exactly what we need. We want every candidate to feel supported and able to do their best. If you need adjustments to our process, we’ll work with you to remove any barriers . Visit our accessibility page for more on this. If you’d like to chat, please contact recruitment@cqc.org.uk. Please note, if you have previously informed us of adjustments you need for interview or within your role these are not carried over and must be discussed for each individual application you make. We promote a workplace where fairness, respect and inclusion are a priority . Diverse teams make our work better, help us deliver our mission and make our culture stronger. See our ED&I page for more about this. e Welcome Applications From Everyone, And Colleagues Can Find Support And Community Among Our Many Employee Networks. This Includes People Of Any Age Sex Gender identity or expression Sexual orientation Religion or belief Ethnicity Disability Values and vision We are guided by our core values, which shape our work and our culture. Excellence – being a high-performing organisation. Caring – treating everyone with dignity and respect. Integrity – doing the right thing. Teamwork – learning from each other to be the best we can. We are a disability confident employer and a carer confident employer. A Note on AI About AI tools can be great for research and refining ideas, but we want to learn about you. If you use AI or Chatbots to help you with your application, keep these points in mind: AI can support research, structuring and refining your writing, but your application must reflect your real skills and experience. Spell-checking and condensing word counts are great ways to use AI effectively. Do not copy and paste AI generated answers. These will not help you stand out; remember we want to hear about your skills and experience. Providing false and insincere examples goes against our core values of honesty and integrity and may lead to your application being withdrawn or termination of your employment.

review_candidates.title: Operations Change Management Officer
review_candidates.description: Ypto zoekt nieuwe collega's, Wil jij onze teams versterken? Ontdek de vacature hieronder en solliciteer. Please apply via the following link: https://www.ypto.be/vacature/?id=2756985 Hoe maak jij mee het verschil? As an Operations Change Management Officer, you support the company-wide rollout and adoption of strategic initiatives led by Operations, including Service Integration and Management (SIAM), Software Asset Management (SAM), IT Asset Management (ITAM), Business Management IT (BMIT), Process Governance implementation, and other operational transformation initiatives. You act as the organizational change bridge between Operations, the wider Ypto/SNCB organizations, business stakeholders, employees, and external partners, ensuring successful understanding, readiness, and adoption of new processes, governance models, technologies, services, roles, and ways of working. You drive the people side of change by combining structured change management with stakeholder engagement, communication, facilitation, learning coordination, resistance management, and adoption monitoring. Working closely with Operations project and program teams, you help ensure that strategic initiatives are successfully introduced, adopted, and sustainably embedded across the wider organization, including the transition towards SIAM and a multi-supplier support model. Wat is jouw rol bij NMBS? As an Operations Change Management Officer, you will take on the following responsibilities: You assess the need for change management support during project and program intake, perform structured change impact and organizational readiness assessments across processes, governance, roles, organization, culture, technology, and ways of working, and identify impacted stakeholder groups, adoption risks, resistance, dependencies, and organizational constraints. You develop and maintain integrated change strategies and plans covering stakeholder engagement, sponsorship, communication, learning, resistance management, and adoption, with clear activities, owners, milestones, and success measures; you integrate these activities into project plans, governance, budgets, risk registers, and reporting, and adapt the approach based on progress, feedback, and adoption results. You translate Operations-led initiatives into practical change interventions for impacted company departments and business stakeholders, support the company-wide rollout of SIAM, SAM, ITAM, BMIT, Process Governance, and other initiatives, maintain an overview of change across the Operations portfolio, and identify overlapping impacts, dependencies, competing priorities, and potential change saturation. You act as the change management liaison between Operations, the wider organization, the business, and external partners; analyze and segment stakeholders; execute targeted engagement approaches; support sponsors, managers, and team leads as visible change leaders; identify and address resistance; provide coaching and practical support; and facilitate alignment across groups with different interests and priorities. You develop and execute targeted communication plans; coordinate clear, consistent, audience-appropriate communications, presentations, guidance, and awareness materials; design and facilitate impact workshops, stakeholder sessions, management briefings, supplier onboarding workshops, and cross-functional alignment activities; and coordinate learning and knowledge needs with HR, Learning, Knowledge Management, and subject-matter experts. You define and monitor adoption objectives, KPIs, stakeholder sentiment, and behavioural change; establish appropriate change governance; report on readiness, engagement, resistance, risks, dependencies, and adoption; escalate material issues through the appropriate governance bodies; support post-implementation embedding and continuous improvement; and coordinate organizational readiness for SIAM and new support suppliers, while operational and administrative onboarding remains with the accountable functions. Waarom is deze job iets voor jou? You hold a Master's degree or have equivalent relevant professional experience. You have at least five years of demonstrable professional experience in organizational change management within complex organizations. You have proven experience supporting organizational, operational, or technology transformations involving multiple functions and stakeholder groups and, preferably, external suppliers or service providers. You have experience in an IT, service management, or technology-enabled transformation environment. You also possess these technical skills: You have experience in organizational change management and have developed and executed change strategies and plans for complex organizational, operational, or technology transformations. You have demonstrable experience in change impact and organizational readiness assessments, stakeholder analysis and engagement, sponsorship, and resistance management. You can translate assessment findings into practical adoption, communication, learning, and engagement activities. You have experience coordinating change across multiple departments, senior stakeholders, delivery teams, and external partners within large or complex organizations. You can develop and execute communication, engagement, and learning plans and facilitate workshops, management sessions, and cross-functional alignment activities. You have experience establishing change governance and monitoring change risks, dependencies, readiness, adoption, and effectiveness, including reporting to program management or senior governance bodies. You have experience in technology-enabled transformations. Knowledge of ITIL, SIAM, ServiceNow, or comparable service management environments is an advantage. You have practical experience with recognized change management methodologies such as Prosci/ADKAR or equivalent methodologies. You are available to work in a hybrid model, including at least two days per week on-site in Brussels. And these soft skills: You communicate clearly in writing and verbally and have strong presentation, workshop design, facilitation, coaching, active listening, and audience-adaptation skills. You translate complex project or program objectives into clear, audience-appropriate interventions and influence stakeholders without formal authority. You apply strong analytical, planning, and coordination skills while managing several initiatives, stakeholder groups, and dependencies simultaneously. You demonstrate organizational awareness, cultural sensitivity, collaboration, adaptability, proactivity, ownership, and the ability to build trust, alignment, and commitment. Asset: You communicate fluently in Dutch, French, and English, spoken and written: Dutch or French at native or at least C1 level, the other language at least B2, and English at least B2. You bring exposure to outsourcing, sourcing transitions, or multi-supplier operating models. You have experience within a public-sector or regulated environment. You hold a formal certification in a recognized change management methodology, such as Prosci/ADKAR or an equivalent methodology, and can demonstrate recent practical application. Diversity Statement Everyone is unique. That's why we believe it’s important that you can be yourself — it makes SNCB stronger. We therefore place great value on diversity and inclusion. Wat mag je van ons verwachten? Choosing SNCB means choosing to contribute to the digital transformation of the Belgian railways. You will have a job with social impact and ample opportunity to make your own contribution. Alongside a healthy work-life balance and a competitive salary, we offer: Hybrid working, with a balanced weekly mix of office and remote work, combined with flexible hours. 40hours/week. 35 days of annual leave. A mobility package with a company car (also available via our mobility plan) or alternative mobility choices, complemented by a public transport season ticket. A target bonus. A comprehensive insurance package, with hospitalisation and dental care for the whole family. Coverage of outpatient medical costs. Group insurance, including a supplementary pension (cafeteria plan). Meal vouchers & eco vouchers. Net allowances for hybrid working and an internet allowance. Waar ga je werken? You will work near Brussels-South station and join the Operations Center Of Excellence team. What’s next? You apply online : https://www.ypto.be/vacature/?id=2756985 We take a close look at your CV and check whether it matches the profile you are looking for. We may call you briefly to ask about your motivation and experience. We invite you for a first (online) HR interview where you can demonstrate your motivation, experience and expectations. In preparation, we will ask you to complete an online personality questionnaire. If the first interview is positive, we invite you for a second technical interview in Brussels. This interview will be with the team, where we’ll discuss the role and how your skills align with the team’s needs. If everything goes well, we will make you a contract offer. You start your new job! We reserve the right to adjust or pause this procedure if necessary. Our recruitment team will select the profiles that best match the job requirements to ensure an optimal fit. Heb je nog vragen? Jobreq 54339 : Ypto recruitment Mail: ypto-recruitment@belgiantrain.be

Basic design checks: HAP load calculations, pipe/duct sizing, hydraulic calculations. Good English for technical review comments and correspondence. Location: New Cairo HQ, with regular project-site visits. Full-time. #Jadeer #MechanicalEngineer #TechnicalOffice #PMO #HVAC #Firefighting #RealEstate #NewCairo #Hiring
